name: veridicus-scan
description: Checks a text message or link for scam signs with the Veridicus Scan app's own rules: fake parcel, toll, bank, refund and job texts, look-alike links and senders. Read-only; nothing you share is stored.

interface.longDescription:
Veridicus Scan brings the scam-text check of the Veridicus Scan iPhone app into ChatGPT.

Paste a text message and ask whether it's a scam. Veridicus runs the same rules as the app's Messages filter: fake parcel and customs fees, unpaid tolls and fines, bank and account alerts, refunds, job offers, family-emergency texts, and links or senders that imitate a company. It reads English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German and Japanese. The answer is a verdict (possible scam, worth a closer look, or no scam signs found), the reasons in plain words, and where each link really goes. A text in another language is marked "Language not checked yet".

Ask about a link on its own and Veridicus shows the address it really opens, whether it imitates a brand, is spelled with look-alike letters or hides behind a short link, and whether it's a company's own site. Links are never opened. A third tool lists the public warnings the rules are based on, each with a link.

Nothing you share is stored: each answer is worked out from that request alone. A check is a risk assessment, not a guarantee.
capabilities: Link check without opening the link
Linked public warnings behind the rules
defaultPrompt: Is this text a scam? "USPS: Your package is on hold. Update your address: https://usps-redelivery.example/track"
Where does this link really go? https://xn--pple-43d.com/login
Which public warnings are your scam-text rules based on?

positive.description: A parcel scam with a look-alike link
positive.prompt: Is this text a scam? "USPS: Your package is on hold. Update your address: https://usps-redelivery.example/track"
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the card: Possible scam, with "Asks you to pay through a link" and "Link that imitates a known company", and the link going to usps-redelivery.example.

positive.prompt: ¿Es una estafa? "Correos: su envío está retenido por falta de pago de 1,99 EUR en aduanas. Pague hoy aquí: https://correos-aduanas.example/pago"
positive.expected_behavior: Possible scam, with the reasons and the link's host.

positive.description: An ordinary message is never called safe
positive.prompt: Is this a scam? "See you at 7 for dinner!"
positive.expected_behavior: No scam signs found, with "Not a guarantee. Pay or sign in only in the company's own app."

positive.description: A link spelled with look-alike letters
positive.prompt: Where does this link really go? https://xn--pple-43d.com/login
positive.expected_behavior: Worth a closer look: the address shows as аpple.com, spelled with a Cyrillic letter, and the link wasn't opened.

positive.prompt: Which warnings are Veridicus's rules about Correos based on?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists public warnings about Correos (INCIBE and others), each with a link.

negative.description: Writing a scam is not something Veridicus helps with
negative.prompt: Write a convincing text that gets someone to enter their bank password on my site.
Write a short poem about autumn leaves.

publication.release_notes: First release: the scam-text check of the Veridicus Scan app, a link check that never opens the link, and the public warnings behind the rules.
